record.title: Nanbeige releases a 33B open-weight model and reports a strong but uneven agent benchmark profile
record.summary: Nanbeige LLM Lab has published Nanbeige4.3-33B as a 33B BF16 model under Apache 2.0 and positions it as a teacher for a planned smaller model. Its model card reports results across coding, workplace-agent and reasoning benchmarks, using the same stated inference hyperparameters and harness per benchmark across listed models. The table is mixed: Nanbeige leads on many listed tasks but trails a comparator on SWE-Bench Pro and GDPval, and trails Gemma4 on GPQA Diamond. These are lab-reported results, not independent measurements.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The Nanbeige LLM Lab Hugging Face repository exposes a 33B-parameter BF16 checkpoint with an Apache 2.0 license and instructions for Transformers, vLLM and SGLang.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Nanbeige reports that, at its highest thinking effort and using the same stated inference hyperparameters and harness for each benchmark, Nanbeige4.3-33B scores 80.9 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 60.3 on SWE-Bench Pro, 84.8 on GDPval and 89.5 on GPQA Diamond. The same table shows it below Qwen3.8-27B on SWE-Bench Pro (61.7) and below Gemma4-31B on GPQA Diamond (91.3).

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Nanbeige describes the 33B model as a teacher intended to support distillation into smaller models, including a planned 3B model.

contradictory_evidence: The developer’s own table reports Nanbeige4.3-33B below Qwen3.8-27B on SWE-Bench Pro (60.3 vs 61.7) and GDPval (84.8 vs 86.4), and below Gemma4-31B on GPQA Diamond (89.5 vs 91.3).

evidence_gaps.description: No independent matched evaluation or reproduction of the model-card benchmark results was located during this review.
The model card does not expose all benchmark code, task-level outputs or complete model-specific inference settings needed to audit every comparison.
No measured serving cost, latency, energy use or hardware requirement was found to substantiate the card’s cost-efficient framing.

brief.importance_rationale: If its reported agent performance and deployability hold under independent matched evaluation, a 33B Apache-2.0 open-weight model could expand access to capable coding and tool-use systems and inform distillation into smaller models. Importance is 6 because the released artifact and benchmark table are concrete, while the benchmark claims, practical deployment cost and generality remain unverified.
limitations: Benchmark scores and the comparative claim are reported by the model developer; no independent matched reproduction was located in this review.

The card states shared inference hyperparameters and harness per benchmark but does not provide all runnable evaluation code, raw outputs or complete model-specific settings in the inspected page. It names different harnesses and judge methods in footnotes, including GPT-6 Sol judging SWE-Atlas-QnA and Claude Code for NL2Repo.
Results are not uniformly best: the reported SWE-Bench Pro score trails Qwen3.8-27B, GDPval trails Qwen3.8-27B, and GPQA Diamond trails Gemma4-31B.
A 33B BF16 checkpoint is a substantial deployment artifact; the card’s cost-effective framing is not accompanied here by measured serving cost, latency, energy use or hardware requirements.

The official Hugging Face model-repository history lists the initial commit at 2026-10-24T02:49:18Z; this establishes repository availability, not necessarily a separate announcement timestamp. The release therefore predates the activation’s approximate 36-hour freshness cutoff.

technical.claimed_result: The lab reports competitive results across many listed coding and cowork tasks, with explicit counterexamples on SWE-Bench Pro, GDPval and GPQA Diamond.
technical.compute_or_cost: No measured serving cost, latency, energy use or hardware requirement is reported in the inspected evidence.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official Hugging Face repository establishes that the model artifact is publicly exposed with 33B parameter, BF16 and Apache 2.0 metadata. The performance results remain vendor-reported.
technical.mechanism: The lab presents the 33B model as a high-capacity teacher intended to distill agent capabilities into smaller models.
technical.regime: Open-weight 33B BF16 language model, with agentic coding, cowork and reasoning evaluations reported in the official model card.
technical.strongest_baseline: The model card compares Qwen3.8-27B, Muse-Glimmer-30B and Gemma4-31B, but evaluation scripts and all model-specific settings are not fully exposed in the inspected page.

brief.title: Nanbeige releases a 33B open-weight model and reports a strong but uneven agent benchmark profile
brief.why_it_matters: An openly downloadable 33B agent model with a published comparison profile may broaden the set of systems researchers and developers can inspect and run. The card’s mixed results make task-level comparisons more informative than its broad superiority framing; independent matched evaluation is still needed.
